first.rationale: Simplified onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but carries a material 30-day retention risk, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify both records before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline, and the verified source showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. This best supports sustainable qualified revenue while also helping activation. Reject promotional pricing this cycle despite competitive pressure because its qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention -12% and failure before first renewal.

final2.rationale: Keep the cycle focused on shortening onboarding. Verified evidence shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. The competitor escalation raises urgency but does not overturn the verified downside of a 40% SMB discount: 30-day retention -12% and cohort loss before first renewal. Pricing-related churn among existing accounts may differ from the tested acquisition use case, but without verification it is too uncertain to displace the stronger sustainable-growth experiment.
